title: What auditors found at the City and other San Francisco public bodies
question: How did the City itself, the school district, City College and the Housing Authority fare when their own handling of federal money was audited?
finding: The Housing Authority's audits reported findings in every one of 7 years (22 in all, 19 marked as repeats). The school district had 3 findings for 2022, the year its auditor gave no opinion on its financial statements. The City's own audit reported 2 findings across 7 years, while the federal money it covers rose from $447 million (2019) to $1.27 billion (2025).
how: Every audit filed with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse under the tax numbers of eight San Francisco public bodies, 2019 to 2025, latest version of each. Findings are counted once per audit and reference number; program names come from the audit's own schedule of federal awards.
limits: These audits test a sample of federal programs each year, not all spending and not local money. Few findings can mean good controls or a narrow sample. The school district and City College are separate governments, not City departments.
